summary.name: Support ticket
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article explaining support tickets (trouble or incident tickets): running reports on a problem, its status, and related data, used mainly in customer support and issue tracking.
summary.what_it_does: This Wikipedia article describes what a support ticket is: a running report on a problem, its status and related data, typically used in customer support call centers and other collaborative settings. It outlines the typical ticket functions, such as entering requests, assigning issues, monitoring handling time, tracking SLAs, generating tickets from monitoring alarms, and keeping a history of changes. It also gives an example workflow from first customer contact through resolution and reopening. The page further compares ticket-tracking systems with bug trackers and mentions uses in government services.
notable: Explains the origin of the term ticket from paper cards in wall-mounted work planning systems
Compares ticket-tracking systems with bug trackers and their shared principles
Describes a step-by-step support ticket workflow from creation to resolution
caveats: Describes a general concept rather than a specific software product
The article notes it needs more citations
